======== docs/concepts.md ========

# Concepts

The domain model of LANventory. Tables and routes are described in
[architecture.md](architecture.md); this page explains what the words mean. Everything described
here is implemented; ideas for later are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Assets

An asset is **one physical item** that you own and can point at: a power strip, a switch, a
cable drum, a monitor. It has

- an inventory number (unique),
- a category,
- a name, and optionally manufacturer, model and serial number,
- a location and a status,
- optional purchase date and a free note,
- the custom fields defined by its category (for example the length of a cable drum).

LANventory tracks **single assets only**. A box of 50 identical patch cables is either 50
assets or not in the inventory at all; there are no quantities or stock levels
(see [ADR 0004](adr/0004-single-assets-only.md)). The benefit is that every item has its own
history, status and inspection record, which DGUV V3 requires anyway.

## Categories and field definitions

A category groups similar assets and defines what you record about them:

- a **name** and an optional **prefix** for inventory numbers (for example `SL`),
- whether **DGUV V3 inspection** is required and the default **interval in months** (default 12),
- any number of **field definitions**.

A field definition has a key, a label, a type, an optional unit, a required flag and an order.
Types:

| Type | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | free text | |
| `number` | decimal number | optional unit, for example `m` for metres |
| `select` | one of a fixed list of options | |
| `bool` | yes / no | |
| `date` | calendar date | |

Values are validated against the type when an asset is saved. They are stored one row per
value ([ADR 0003](adr/0003-configurable-fields-as-eav.md)), so they can be filtered and
searched. Numbers are numbers: the unit lives in the field definition, not in the value.
Seeded templates (power strip, cable drum, power cable, network cable, switch, monitor,
PC/server; German names) are created once on first start and can be edited or deleted; deleted
ones do not come back.

Rules of the field editor: a field's key is fixed after creation; its type cannot change while
values exist; a select option that is in use cannot be removed; deleting a field deletes its
values; a category cannot be deleted while assets use it. Numbers accept a comma as decimal
separator and are stored with a dot.

The category of an existing asset can be changed in the edit form (or via the API): values move
to fields of the new category with the same key when they are valid there, the others are dropped
and listed before saving; the inventory number and the inspections stay.

## Inventory numbers

Numbers are generated from `inventory.number_format`, default `{prefix}-{seq:05}`:
`{prefix}` is the category prefix, `{seq:05}` a running number padded to five digits, giving
`SL-00042`. The format must contain `{seq}`.

- **Without prefix:** the prefix is optional. A category without prefix drops `{prefix}` and the
  separator after it (`-`, `_`, `/`, `.` or a space), so the default format gives `00042`.
  Categories with a prefix have one sequence per prefix; all categories without prefix share one.
- **Plain running numbers:** a format without `{prefix}`, for example `{seq:04}` for `0001`,
  `0002`, …, uses a single sequence for all categories, whatever their prefixes.
- **Existing numbers:** numbers that are already taken (entered by hand or imported) are skipped,
  so after importing `0001`–`0250` the next generated number is `0251`.

A number can be **overridden manually** when
creating an asset, for example to adopt an existing labelling scheme; it must stay unique.
Changing the format later, or a category's prefix, does not renumber existing assets. Numbers
are reserved in the same transaction that creates the asset; a number that is already taken
(for example a manual one) is skipped. A manual number cannot be changed after creation.

## Locations

Locations are a **flat list** such as "Storage 1" and "Storage 2", with an optional
description. There is no hierarchy (room, shelf, box). An asset has at most one location.

## Status

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `active` | in use or in stock, available |
| `defective` | broken, waiting for repair; failed inspections lead here |
| `retired` | taken out of service on purpose; kept for the records |
| `lost` | cannot be found |

Assets are not deleted when they leave the inventory; they are retired or marked lost, so the
history stays intact. Status changes are written to the asset's change history.

## DGUV V3 inspections

In Germany, portable electrical equipment used in a workplace or at events must be inspected
periodically according to DGUV Vorschrift 3, using the test procedures of DIN VDE 0701-0702.
LANventory supports the paperwork:

- A category can require inspection and sets the **interval** in months (default 12). A single
  asset can override the interval.
- An **inspection** records the date, the inspector's name (prefilled with the current user; may
  be an external electrician), the result (**pass** or **fail**, decided by the inspector), the
  protection class, whether the visual inspection and the functional test passed, the
  **reason** (before first use, repeat inspection, after repair; the form preselects "repeat"
  for an asset that has inspections, "initial" otherwise; empty = not recorded), the
  measurements (protective conductor resistance in ohm, insulation resistance in megohm,
  protective conductor or leakage current in milliampere with its measuring method direct,
  differential or alternative (substitute leakage current), and the **touch current** in
  milliampere; all optional, non-negative, comma or dot), the **test device** with its ID or
  serial number and calibration date, and a remark. The applied interval and the next due date
  are stored with it. The form prefills the test device, ID and calibration date from the
  user's last inspection and shows a non-blocking hint when the calibration ended before the
  inspection date.
- **Readings beyond the instrument's range.** A measurement may start with `>` or `<` (space,
  comma or dot decimals allowed): `>299` MOhm, `< 0,01` mA. The number is stored as a number and
  the qualifier next to it (`pe_resistance_cmp`, `insulation_cmp`, `leakage_cmp`, `touch_cmp`:
  empty, `<` or `>`); it is displayed as "> 299 MΩ". Guidance compares the number as it is (">299"
  insulation is not low, "<0,01" leakage is not high). The API takes numbers plus the `*_cmp`
  properties, and also a string such as `">299"` for the measurement.
- The **next due date** is the inspection date plus the interval in calendar months; a day that
  does not exist in the target month moves to its last day (31 January + 1 month = 28 or 29
  February). Due states: *overdue* when the due date is before today, *due soon* when it is
  today or within the next 30 days, *never inspected* without any inspection. Retired and lost
  assets, and categories without DGUV, are not listed as due; defective assets are.
- **Inspections are records**: they cannot be edited. Only an admin can delete one (audited).
- Only users with the `can_inspect` flag can record inspections; the flag is independent of the
  role. Only assets of categories that require DGUV V3 and are not retired or lost can be
  inspected. A failed inspection can set the asset to defective in the same step (opt-in, off by default); a passed one
  can set a defective asset back to active.
- **Guidance hints.** LANventory never decides pass or fail. It only shows a hint next to
  values outside simplified limits in the spirit of DIN VDE 0701-0702: protective conductor
  resistance above 0.3 ohm, insulation resistance below 1 megohm (class I) or 2 megohm (class
  II), protective conductor / leakage current above 3.5 mA (class I), touch current above 0.5 mA
  (classes I and II). These limits are simplified and live in one place (`internal/store/dguv.go`); the
  standard's detailed rules (for example the cable length) apply and the inspector decides.
- A **protocol** (`/inspections/{id}/print`) can be printed per inspection; the list of
  inspections can be exported as CSV with the same filters.

**Disclaimer:** LANventory documents inspections and reminds you of due dates. It does not
perform or validate them and does not replace a qualified electrician (Elektrofachkraft).
You remain responsible for the safety of your equipment and for complying with the rules that
apply to you.

## CSV import and export

**Export.** `/assets.csv` (every role) downloads the assets of the list with the same filters
and sort (`q`, `category`, `location`, `status`, `f_<key>`, `sort`, `dir`), all matching rows up
to 50 000. UTF-8 without BOM, comma, CRLF, one header row. Columns, in this order:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `inventory_no`, `category`, `category_prefix`, `name`, `serial_no`, `manufacturer`, `model` | as stored |
| `location` | location name |
| `status` | `active`, `defective`, `retired`, `lost` |
| `purchase_date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `dguv_interval_months` | the asset's own override, empty if none |
| `note` | free text |
| `last_inspected_on`, `next_due` | latest inspection; `next_due` empty without DGUV requirement or inspection |
| `field:<key>` | one column per custom field of the categories in the result (sorted by category name, then position; empty where the field does not apply); numbers with a dot, booleans `1`/`0`, dates `YYYY-MM-DD` |

Every cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR gets a leading apostrophe so that
spreadsheets do not run it as a formula (this also applies to the inspection export); the
import removes that apostrophe again.

**Import.** Editors and admins upload a CSV file (at most 5 MB, 20 000 rows) at
`/assets/import`; the first row must be the header. Delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab) and
encoding (UTF-8, Windows-1252, as written by Excel on German Windows) are detected unless
chosen. The mapping step assigns each column to *ignore*, a core column or `field:<key>`
(pre-selected by our export headers, German names such as Inventarnummer, Kategorie,
Bezeichnung, Seriennummer, Hersteller, Modell, Standort, Status, Kaufdatum, Bemerkung, and field
labels such as "Länge"). Options: default category and location, "all or nothing" or "skip invalid
rows", create missing locations, and what to do with an existing inventory number (skip or
update). The preview lists the first 200 rows with the action (create, update, skip, error) and a
message per faulty cell, then everything is written in one transaction.

Accepted values: category by name or prefix; status in English or German (aktiv, defekt,
ausgemustert, verloren); booleans 1/0, ja/nein, yes/no, true/false, x; numbers with comma or dot;
dates `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD.MM.YYYY`. Everything passes the same validation as the forms. An empty
inventory number is generated; a number that occurs twice in the file is an error for the later
rows. With *update*, an explicit category must match the existing asset; mapped empty cells clear
values. The export of the asset list can be imported again unchanged.

**Past inspections in the CSV import.** Optional inspection columns turn a row into asset plus
one inspection, like a row of an electrician's inspection protocol: `inspected_on`,
`inspector_name`, `result`, `reason`, `protection_class`, `visual_ok`, `function_ok`,
`pe_resistance_ohm`, `insulation_mohm`, `leakage_ma`, `leakage_method`, `touch_ma`,
`test_device`, `test_device_id`, `test_device_calibrated_until`, `remark`. German headers are
mapped automatically (Prüfdatum, Prüfer, Ergebnis, Prüfanlass, Schutzklasse,
Sichtprüfung/Besichtigung, Funktionsprüfung, RPE (protective conductor resistance), Riso
(insulation), ISL/IPE (protective conductor current), Verfahren/Messverfahren, IB (touch current),
Prüfgerät, Prüfmittel-ID, Kalibriert bis, Bemerkung; in a file with inspection columns "Bemerkung" is the inspection's
remark, otherwise the asset's note). Values: result `pass`/`fail` or bestanden, nicht bestanden,
i.O., nicht i.O., ja, nein; class `I`, `II`, `III` or "SK I"; method Dir, Diff, AM (or direkt,
Differenzstrom, Ersatzableitstrom); reason in English or German words (Wiederholungsprüfung …);
measurements as `>299`, `<0,01`, with `-` or empty meaning not measured. Rules: a row with
`inspected_on` and `result` records an inspection of the created or updated asset (existing
numbers only in *update* mode); the category must require DGUV V3 (else a row error); inspector,
date and result are required; the next due date is computed from the interval as usual; an
identical inspection (same asset, date and result) is not duplicated, so a re-import is
idempotent; the asset status is **not** changed by a failed result (the `status` column can set
it); retired and lost assets may receive past inspections. One row holds one inspection, so
several inspections of one device need several import runs. Only users with the `can_inspect`
flag can import these columns; for others the mapping step refuses them. The preview and the
result page show the number of inspections recorded (and already present); audit entries
`inspection.create` with `via: import`.

## Data export and import (JSON)

The CSV import and export handle the asset list. To **move the whole inventory** from one
instance to another (for example from a test instance to production) there is a second, lossless
format: one JSON file with locations, categories with their field definitions, assets with
custom field values and all DGUV inspections.

**Export.** Admins download it at `/admin/data` (`GET /admin/data/export.json`, file
`lanventory-export-YYYY-MM-DD.json`), or run `lanventory data export [-o file]`. Layout:

```json
{"format": "lanventory-export", "version": 1, "exported_at": "…", "app_version": "…",
 "locations": [{"name": "", "description": ""}],
 "categories": [{"name": "", "prefix": "", "dguv_required": true, "dguv_interval_months": 24,
                 "fields": [{"key": "", "label": "", "type": "number", "unit": "", "options": [], "required": false}]}],
 "assets": [{"inventory_no": "", "category": "<name>", "name": "", "serial_no": "", "manufacturer": "",
             "model": "", "location": "<name or empty>", "status": "active", "note": "",
             "purchase_date": null, "dguv_interval_months": null, "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…",
             "fields": {"<key>": "<value as stored>"},
             "inspections": [{"inspected_on": "", "inspector_name": "", "recorded_by": "<username or empty>",
                              "result": "pass", "protection_class": "", "visual_ok": true, "function_ok": true,
                              "pe_resistance_ohm": null, "insulation_mohm": null, "leakage_ma": null,
                              "test_device": "", "remark": "", "interval_months": 12, "next_due": "", "created_at": "…",
                              "pe_resistance_cmp": "", "insulation_cmp": "", "leakage_cmp": "", "leakage_method": "",
                              "touch_ma": null, "touch_cmp": "", "reason": "", "test_device_id": "",
                              "test_device_calibrated_until": ""}]}]}
```

The last nine inspection properties (qualifiers, method, touch current, reason, test device ID and
calibration date) are optional: files without them still import (empty values).

Values are exported as stored (booleans `"1"`/`"0"`, numbers with a dot), fields in their
position order, assets sorted by inventory number, inspections by date, timestamps RFC 3339 UTC.
Users, sessions, API tokens, settings, the audit log and all secrets are **not** exported.

**Import.** Admins upload the file at `/admin/data` (at most 5 MB) or run
`lanventory data import [--dry-run] [--on-conflict skip|abort] [--update-categories=false] <file>`. The web UI first shows a
preview (a dry run in a rolled-back transaction: what would be created, skipped inventory numbers,
warnings, problems); only the confirmation writes, in one transaction, all or nothing. The
export, the upload and the confirmation need a recent authentication.

- Unknown `format` or `version` is refused. Unknown JSON keys are refused.
- **Locations** are matched by name (case-insensitive); missing ones are created, existing ones
  keep their description.
- **Categories** are matched by name (case-insensitive). A missing category is created with its
  prefix, DGUV settings and fields; a prefix already used by a *different* category is a conflict.
  For an existing category, **"adopt the settings of existing categories"** (default on, CLI
  `--update-categories`) takes prefix, DGUV flag and interval, and label, unit and required flag
  of matching fields from the file – a fresh instance has seeded template categories (for example
  a 12-month interval) that would otherwise keep their defaults; a required flag is not switched on
  for a category that already has assets. With the option off, the existing category keeps its
  settings and the differences are reported as warnings. Its fields are matched by key, missing fields are added (as optional when the category already has assets),
  missing select options are added, and a field with the same key but another type is a conflict.
- **Assets** are matched by inventory number (case-insensitive). Existing numbers are skipped and
  listed (`skip`, default) or abort the whole import (`abort`); existing assets are never changed.
  New assets keep their number, status (also retired and lost), `created_at` and `updated_at`.
  Numbers are not generated; the running number simply skips taken numbers later. Values pass the
  same validation as the forms; a problem is reported with its place, for example
  `assets[12].fields.length_m`. A required flag is not enforced on import, so that assets that
  predate a required field can be moved.
- **Inspections** are imported only for newly created assets, as records with the stored interval
  and next due date (not recomputed). Result, protection class, dates and measurement ranges are
  validated; the "asset must be active and inspectable" rule does not apply. `recorded_by` is the
  user with that name if it exists, else the importing user (none for the command line).
- Audit: one `asset.create` entry per created asset (details `via: data_import`) and one
  `data.import` summary; the export writes `data.export`.

**Moving data.** Export on the old instance, import on the new one (users are created there
separately). A new instance already has the seeded categories; categories with the same name are
merged as described above. Run a dry run first.

## Bulk edit

Editors and admins change several assets at once. In the asset list they tick rows (the header
checkbox selects the page; "select all N matches of the filter" selects every asset matching the
current filter, at most 1000), then "Edit selected". The form shows the selected inventory numbers
and, for every property, a "change" tick plus the input; only ticked properties change. Properties:
category, location (– clears it), status, manufacturer, model, purchase date, DGUV interval (empty =
category default), note (replace, or append as a new line) and custom fields. Name, serial number
and inventory number are deliberately not bulk-editable.

- **Custom fields** can be changed when all selected assets end up in one category: they share one,
  or the category change is ticked (choose the category and press "Load fields"; the fields of the
  target category appear). An empty value clears the field. A key the asset's category lacks is an
  error for that asset.
- **Category move** works as for a single asset: values carry over to fields with the same key when
  valid, the others are lost (listed in the preview), required fields of the target category must
  be filled (set them in the same form).
- **Preview and apply.** The preview is a dry run: per changed asset the changes old → new, lost
  values and, if the change is invalid for some assets, the errors grouped per field and the assets
  concerned. Nothing is written until "Apply"; the whole change is one transaction (all or
  nothing). Assets that already have the values are left alone. Each changed asset gets an
  `asset.update` audit entry with `via: bulk`; the API uses `via: api_bulk`.
- **API.** `PATCH /api/v1/assets` with `ids`, `changes` (API names, `fields` by key, `note_append`)
  and `dry_run`; validation errors are keyed `"<asset id>.<field>"`.

## Roles


| Role | May |
|---|---|
| `viewer` | read everything |
| `editor` | additionally create and change assets and locations |
| `admin` | additionally manage categories and their fields, delete assets, manage users and see the audit log |

`can_inspect` allows recording inspections for any role that can log in. Authorization is
always checked on the server.

**API tokens** act as their owner with scopes `read:assets`, `write:assets`, `read:inspections`
and `write:inspections`; a token can never do more than its owner may at that moment (writing
needs editor, deleting assets or inspections admin, recording inspections `can_inspect`).
Categories are read-only in the API. See [api.md](api.md).

## Units and formats

Timestamps are Unix seconds (UTC) in the database and RFC 3339 UTC in the API. Dates in the UI
follow the user's language (German `DD.MM.YYYY`, English `YYYY-MM-DD`; form inputs and CSV use
`YYYY-MM-DD`), and so do decimal separators (German comma, English dot; both are accepted as
input). Measures are plain numbers; the unit comes from the field
definition or, for inspections, is fixed (ohm, megohm, milliampere).


======== docs/architecture.md ========

# Architecture

LANventory is one Go binary: an HTTP server with a server-rendered web UI (`html/template`,
a small `app.js`, no inline scripts), a SQLite database and a command line. Read this file
instead of re-exploring the code.

## Packages

```
llms.go                    embeds llms.txt (served at GET /llms.txt)
internal/api/              REST API /api/v1: api.go (routes, token/session auth, problem+json,
                           audit), helpers.go, locations/categories/assets/bulk/inspections/me.go,
                           docs.go (HTML docs, spec), openapi.yaml (embedded, single source)
tools/e2e/                 browser end-to-end tests (Selenium + system Chromium):
                           passkey_e2e.py, inventory_e2e.py, inspection_e2e.py, api_e2e.py,
                           import_e2e.py, bulk_e2e.py (see testing.md)
tools/gendocs/             generates docs/configuration.md, config.schema.json, llms-full.txt
                           from internal/config/config.go; a test checks they are current
cmd/lanventory/            main.go
cmd/lanventory/cmd/        cobra commands: root.go (config, logging, env), server.go,
                           admin.go (config init, migrate, backup, user …, user reset-mfa,
                           mfa policy), data.go (data export, data import)
pkg/version/               Version, Commit, BuildDate (set with ldflags)
internal/app/              App (config, DB, key, logger), client IP, session context,
                           SameOrigin, Audit, SecurityHeaders (CSP), RequestLog
internal/auth/             Argon2id, random tokens, LoginLimiter, RateLimiter
internal/secret/           AES-256-GCM with associated data, keyed MAC (subkey), secret.key
internal/mfa/              TOTP (RFC 6238), recovery codes, WebAuthn relying party from
                           public_url, in-memory ceremony store
internal/config/           YAML config, defaults, validation, Example (= docs/config.example.yaml)
internal/store/            SQLite (modernc), goose migrations, users, sessions, audit log,
                           mfa.go (TOTP, recovery codes, passkeys, settings, MFA policy)
                           locations.go, categories.go (with field definitions), assets.go,
                           assetlist.go (search, filters, sorting, paging, counts, audit by
                           object), numbers.go (number format and sequence), seed.go (category
                           templates), validate.go (ValidationError, value normalization)
                           dguv.go (next due date, due state, guidance limits; pure functions),
                           inspections.go (inspections, due overview, list/export queries)
                           assetexport.go (asset CSV export query), csvfile.go (CSV decoding and
                           parsing for the import), import.go (mapping suggestion, import run),
                           dataexport.go (JSON format types, ExportData), dataimport.go
                           (ParseDataExport, ImportData: full transfer incl. inspections),
                           tokens.go (API tokens)
                           bulk.go (BulkUpdateAssets: change many assets in one transaction,
                           AssetIDsByFilter, AssetsByIDs)
  migrations/sqlite/       00001_init.sql, 00002_mfa.sql, 00003_inventory.sql,
                           00004_inspections.sql, 00005_api_tokens.sql,
                           00006_inspection_details.sql
internal/web/              chi router, handlers, i18n.go, templates/, static/
```

## Request flow

1. `chi` middlewares: `Recoverer`, `RequestLog`, `GetHead`.
2. `GET /health` answers JSON `{"status":"ok","version":"…"}` (no login, no secrets).
   `GET /llms.txt` serves the embedded `llms.txt` as `text/plain` (public, `web.Server.LLMs`).
3. Everything else passes `SecurityHeaders` (CSP and friends) and `SessionMiddleware`, which
   resolves the cookie `lv_session` (hashed with SHA-256, looked up in `sessions`), extends the
   session after half of its lifetime and puts session and user into the request context.
4. `internal/web` routes:
   - Public: `/login`, `/static/*`, `POST /login/passkey/{options,finish}` (passwordless; checked
     with the login page's double-submit token `lv_login` sent as `X-Login-CSRF` + `SameOrigin`).
   - Pending sessions (password accepted, second factor missing; `SessionMiddleware` puts them
     into the context with `app.PendingUser`, so `app.User` stays nil): `requirePending` +
     `csrf` for `/login/mfa`, `/login/mfa/passkey/{options,finish}`, `/login/mfa/cancel`.
   - Everything else: `requireLogin`, `csrf` (form field `_csrf` or header `X-CSRF-Token`, plus
     `SameOrigin`) and `enforceMFA` (redirects to `/account/security` when the MFA policy requires
     a second factor the user lacks; enrollment routes are exempt). `/admin/*` additionally uses
     `requireRole(admin)`. `requireRecentAuth` (session `auth_at` younger than 10 minutes, else
     `/reauth`) guards `/account/{totp,recovery,passkeys}/*` POSTs, `POST /admin/security` and
     `POST /admin/users/{id}/mfa-reset`.
   - Inventory (all behind `requireLogin`): `GET /assets`, `/assets/{id}`, `/locations`,
     `/categories`, `/categories/{id}` for every role. `requireRole(editor)`: `GET /assets/new`,
     `POST /assets`, `GET /assets/{id}/edit`, `POST /assets/{id}`, `POST /locations`,
     `POST /locations/{id}[/delete]`. `requireRole(admin)`: `POST /assets/{id}/delete`,
     `POST /categories[/{id}[/delete]]`, `POST /categories/{id}/fields[/{fid}[/delete|/move]]`.
     `GET /assets` answers htmx requests (`HX-Request: true`, not a history restore) with the
     `asset_fragment` template only (`Server.renderFragment`); `Page.HTMX` makes the layout load
     htmx and its config on that page only.
   - Bulk edit (`requireRole(editor)`): `POST /assets/bulk/edit` (form; the selection comes as
     repeated `id` fields or, with `all_matches=1`, as the list filter `filter` that is resolved
     with `AssetIDsByFilter`, at most 1000, and is carried on as hidden ids), `POST
     /assets/bulk/preview` (dry run through `store.BulkUpdateAssets`, errors grouped per field),
     `POST /assets/bulk/apply` (real run; audit `asset.update` per changed asset with `via: bulk`;
     redirect to `/assets?ok=bulk&n=<changed>`). Form input travels as `chg_<property>` (tick) and
     `v_<property>`, custom fields as `chg_f_<key>`/`v_f_<key>`, `note_mode` (replace/append).
     `handlers_bulk.go`, templates `bulk_form.html`, `bulk_preview.html`; the list's checkboxes,
     select-all and counter are bound by delegation in `app.js` (`data-bulk-*` attributes) and the
     bulk `<form id="bulk-form">` lives outside the htmx-swapped `#results`.
   - CSV (behind `requireLogin`): `GET /assets.csv` for every role (list filters, `csvWriter` with
     the formula guard shared with `/inspections.csv`). Import for editors and admins
     (`requireRole(editor)`): `GET /assets/import` (upload form), `POST /assets/import`
     (multipart upload; answers with the mapping page), `POST /assets/import/map` (mapping page
     again), `POST /assets/import/preview`, `POST /assets/import/confirm`. `importBody` (before
     `csrf`) limits and parses the upload body so that the CSRF check can read the form. The parsed
     upload is kept in `Server.imports` (`importStates`, memory only: token bound to user and
     session, one per user, at most 16, TTL 30 minutes, claim flag); the steps carry only the
     token. `store.RunImport` plans (rolled-back transaction) and performs the import (one
     transaction, `createAsset`/`updateAsset` shared with `CreateAsset`/`UpdateAsset`).
   - Data export/import (admins; `requireRole(admin)` plus `requireRecentAuth("/admin/data")` on
     all of them): `GET /admin/data` (page), `GET /admin/data/export.json` (download
     `lanventory-export-YYYY-MM-DD.json`, audit `data.export`), `POST /admin/data/import`
     (multipart upload, answers with the preview; `importBody` limits it to 5 MB like the CSV
     upload), `POST /admin/data/preview` (dry run again with the chosen conflict mode),
     `POST /admin/data/confirm` (import; audit `asset.create` per asset with `via: data_import`
     and `data.import`). The parsed upload lives in `Server.imports` like the CSV upload (a state
     holds `Table` or `Data`; the CSV wizard refuses data tokens). `store.ImportData` runs in one
     transaction and writes inspections as records (no recomputation); `DryRun` rolls back.
   - DGUV V3 (behind `requireLogin`): `GET /inspections`, `/inspections.csv`, `/inspections/due`,
     `/inspections/{id}`, `/inspections/{id}/print` for every role. `requireInspector`
     (`can_inspect`, independent of the role): `GET /assets/{id}/inspections/new`,
     `POST /assets/{id}/inspections`. `requireRole(admin)`: `POST /inspections/{id}/delete`.
     `/inspections/due` answers htmx requests with the `due_results` fragment like `/assets`. The
     protocol page (`protocol.html`, parsed on its own, `Server.renderProtocol`) has no layout and
     no script and loads only `static/print.css`.
   - Passkey endpoints speak JSON (`webauthn.js` posts with `X-CSRF-Token`/`X-Login-CSRF`); a
     running ceremony is identified by the short-lived cookie `lv_wa`.
   - REST API (`internal/api`, mounted at `/api` in `server.go` behind `SecurityHeaders` and
     `SessionMiddleware`, outside the web router): `/api/` docs, `/api/openapi.json|yaml`,
     `/api/v1/*`. Authentication per request: `Authorization: Bearer lvk_…` (hash lookup,
     revoked/expired/disabled owner → 401, per-token rate limit) or a full session (unsafe
     methods need `X-CSRF-Token` + same origin; MFA policy enforced; pending sessions rejected).
     Each route declares a `need` (scope, minimum role, `can_inspect`); a token needs the scope
     AND the owner's current rights. Errors are `application/problem+json`.
5. Handlers load data from `store`, build a `Page` and render `layout` with the page template.
   Texts come from `i18n.go` via `Page.T`.

Roles are ordered viewer < editor < admin (`store.RoleLevel`, `User.Can(role)`). The flag
`can_inspect` is independent of the role.

## Data model

Timestamps are Unix seconds (UTC). Migration `00001_init.sql`:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `users` | `id`, `username` (unique, case-insensitive), `password_hash` (Argon2id PHC string), `role` (`viewer`, `editor`, `admin`), `can_inspect`, `theme` (`auto`, `light`, `dark`), `lang` (`de`, `en`), `disabled`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_login_at` |
| `sessions` | `id` (SHA-256 of the cookie value), `user_id` (cascade), `csrf_token`, `created_at`, `expires_at` |
| `audit_log` | `id`, `ts`, `user_id` (nullable, set to NULL when the user is deleted), `action`, `object_type`, `object_id`, `details` (JSON text; keys `actor` and `ip` are used by the UI; never secrets) |

Migration `00002_mfa.sql` (phase 2):

| Table / column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `users.totp_secret` | TOTP secret, AES-GCM with associated data `totp|<user id>`; NULL = none; set with `totp_enabled_at` NULL = enrollment pending |
| `users.totp_enabled_at`, `users.totp_last_step` | activation time; last accepted time step (replay protection) |
| `users.webauthn_handle` | random 32-byte WebAuthn user handle (unique), created with the first passkey |
| `sessions.pending`, `sessions.auth_at` | second factor still missing (5-minute session); time of the last full authentication |
| `recovery_codes` | `user_id`, `code_mac` (hex HMAC-SHA256 under a subkey of `secret.key`), `created_at`, `used_at` |
| `webauthn_credentials` | `user_id`, `credential_id` (unique), `name`, `credential` (JSON of `webauthn.Credential`: public key, flags, sign count), `created_at`, `last_used_at` |
| `settings` | `key`, `value`, `updated_at`; currently `mfa_policy` (`off`, `admins`, `all`) |

Migration `00003_inventory.sql` (phase 3):

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `locations` | `id`, `name` (unique, case-insensitive), `description`, timestamps |
| `categories` | `id`, `name` (unique, case-insensitive), `prefix` (`A–Z0–9`, 0–8; unique unless empty, partial index), `dguv_required`, `dguv_interval_months` (1–120, default 12), timestamps |
| `category_fields` | `id`, `category_id` (cascade), `key` (unique per category), `label`, `type` (`text`, `number`, `select`, `bool`, `date`), `unit`, `options` (JSON array, select only), `required`, `position` |
| `assets` | `id`, `inventory_no` (unique, case-insensitive), `category_id` (restrict), `name`, `serial_no`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `location_id` (restrict, nullable), `status` (`active`, `defective`, `retired`, `lost`), `note`, `purchase_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `dguv_interval_months` (override), timestamps; indexes on category, location, status, serial number |
| `asset_field_values` | `asset_id` (cascade), `field_id` (cascade), `value` (normalized text); primary key `(asset_id, field_id)` |
| `number_sequences` | `prefix`, `next`: running number per category prefix; `''` is shared by categories without prefix and by formats without `{prefix}` |

`settings` additionally holds `seeded_categories` (category templates were created once). The
asset history is not a table: it is the audit log filtered by `object_type = 'asset'`; `asset.*`
entries carry `changes` (`{field: [old, new]}`) in their details.

Migration `00004_inspections.sql` (phase 4):

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `dguv_inspections` | `id`, `asset_id` (cascade), `inspected_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `inspector_name` (free text, may be external), `recorded_by` (user, set NULL on delete), `result` (`pass`, `fail`), `protection_class` (`I`, `II`, `III`, nullable), `visual_ok`, `function_ok`, `pe_resistance_ohm`, `insulation_mohm`, `leakage_ma` (REAL, nullable, non-negative), `test_device`, `remark`, `interval_months` (the interval applied), `next_due` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `created_at`; indexes `(asset_id, inspected_on)` and `(inspected_on)` |

Inspections are never updated. The state of an asset derives from its latest inspection
(`inspected_on`, then `id`); deleting that inspection falls back to the previous one. Audit
entries `inspection.create` and `inspection.delete` (object type `inspection`); status changes
caused by an inspection are `asset.update` entries with `via: inspection`. Configuration
`organization.name` is printed on protocols.

Migration `00006_inspection_details.sql` (step 6.6) extends `dguv_inspections` (all with defaults, so
existing rows stay valid):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pe_resistance_cmp`, `insulation_cmp`, `leakage_cmp`, `touch_cmp` | comparison qualifier of the reading: `''` (exact), `'<'` or `'>'` (CHECK) |
| `touch_ma` | touch current, REAL, nullable, non-negative (0–1000); `leakage_ma` stays the protective conductor / leakage current |
| `leakage_method` | `''`, `direct`, `differential`, `alternative` (CHECK) |
| `reason` | inspection reason: `''` (not recorded), `initial`, `repeat`, `repair` (CHECK) |
| `test_device_id` | test device ID or serial number (max 100) |
| `test_device_calibrated_until` | `YYYY-MM-DD`, nullable |

The CSV import (`store/import.go`) writes inspections through the same `insertInspection` as the form
and the JSON import; its inspection columns need `ImportOptions.AllowInspections` (the user's
`can_inspect`).

Migration `00005_api_tokens.sql` (phase 5):

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `api_tokens` | `id`, `name`, `prefix` (first 8 characters, for display), `token_hash` (unique, SHA-256 hex), `scopes` (space-separated), `user_id` (owner, cascade), `created_at`, `expires_at` (nullable), `last_used_at`, `revoked` |

Web routes for tokens: `GET /account/tokens`, `POST /account/tokens` (`requireRecentAuth`),
`POST /account/tokens/{id}/revoke` (own tokens), `GET /admin/tokens`, `POST
/admin/tokens/{id}/revoke` (admin). Audit entries `token.create`, `token.revoke`; changes made
through the API carry `via: api` (`via: api_bulk` for `PATCH /api/v1/assets`) and `token_id` in their details. Config keys `api.rate_limit`
and `api.rate_burst`.

## Security mechanisms

See [security.md](security.md). In short: Argon2id, lockout, hashed session IDs, `SameSite=Strict`
cookies, CSRF token plus same-origin check, strict CSP, escaped output, encrypted secrets.

## Tests

How to run the unit, handler and browser end-to-end tests: [testing.md](testing.md).

`go test ./...` – unit tests for auth, secret, mfa (RFC 6238 vectors, skew, replay, recovery
codes, relying-party URL rules, ceremonies), config and store; web tests drive the real
router through `httptest` (login, lockout, CSRF and origin, roles, user management, last-admin
protection, security headers, template keys and absence of inline code; inventory: role
checks for every route group, location and category/field editor flows, form validation and
XSS escaping, history after create/edit/status change, list filters, URL round trip, htmx
fragment versus full page; store tests cover CRUD, constraints, seeding once, value
normalization, number generation (also 20 concurrent creates), search/filter queries, type-change
and delete protection; TOTP login with replay
and recovery codes, pending sessions, MFA policy, re-authentication, admin MFA reset, passkey
endpoint guards). The WebAuthn ceremony itself is tested in a browser: `tools/e2e/passkey_e2e.py` (Selenium,
Chrome DevTools virtual authenticator; passkey registration, passwordless login, passkey as
second factor, passkey re-authentication, TOTP enrollment and login); the other end-to-end scripts
cover the inventory, inspections, the API and the CSV import. The race detector runs
in CI only. Phase 4: store tests cover next-due arithmetic (month ends, leap years, override), due
state boundaries, exclusions, inspection creation with the status change in one transaction,
refusals, delete and cascade and the list/export filters; web tests cover the `can_inspect`
check (403, also for admins; viewers with the flag allowed), refusals, validation re-render,
guidance hints, the script-free protocol, CSV columns, escaping and formula protection, the
htmx fragment of the due page, dashboard counts equal to the overview and German number and date
formatting.

Phase 5: `internal/api` tests (`spec_test.go`, `validate_test.go`, `api_test.go`, fixture in
`fixture_test.go`) check routes against `openapi.yaml`, validate every response (and the request
bodies of successful calls) with kin-openapi, and cover scopes, owner role changes, token states,
hash-only storage, rate limit, sessions with CSRF/pending MFA/MFA policy, validation errors,
by-number lookup, number generation, inspection rules and audit entries; `web_tokens_test.go`
covers the token pages.

Phase 6: store tests cover delimiter sniffing, encodings (Windows-1252 bytes, UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16),
header auto-mapping, value parsing, duplicates, generated numbers, skip vs update, category
mismatch, all-or-nothing vs skip-invalid, locations; web tests cover roles (viewers: 403 for the
import, export allowed), the 5 MB limit, CSRF, token binding to user and session, state expiry,
the full flow with a Windows-1252 file, escaped cells in the preview, audit entries, export
columns/escaping/guard/filters/sort and the export → import round trip.

Bulk edit (step 6.9): store tests (`bulk_test.go`) cover location/status for several assets,
simple fields, note append, custom values by key, category moves with carried and lost values,
required fields of the target category (errors for exactly the affected assets, nothing written),
dry run, the 1000 limit, unknown ids and the filter resolution; web tests (`web_bulk_test.go`)
cover roles (viewers: no checkboxes, 403), the form → preview → apply flow with CSRF, "all
matches" and its limit, and audit entries with `via: bulk`; API tests cover `PATCH
/api/v1/assets` (success, dry run, per-asset errors, request errors, scope and role) and the spec
conformance.

Data export/import (step 6.8): store tests cover the round trip (export → import into a fresh
database → export again, equal except `exported_at`; with and without seeded categories),
conflicts (prefix, field type), `skip` versus `abort`, dry run, value paths in errors, unknown
format and version; web tests cover admin-only access, download headers, CSRF, recent
authentication, token binding and the upload → preview → confirm flow with audit entries.

## Third-party code

Go: `go-webauthn/webauthn` is pinned to v0.15.0, the last release that supports Go 1.24
(v0.16+ needs Go 1.25); Dependabot ignores newer versions until the toolchain moves.
`skip2/go-qrcode` renders the TOTP QR code. `getkin/kin-openapi` v0.133.0 is a test-only
dependency (response validation against the OpenAPI document).

## Third-party files

`internal/web/static/htmx.min.js` is htmx 2.0.4, vendored without changes. Only the asset list
loads it (`Page.HTMX`), with `<meta name="htmx-config">` turning off indicator styles, eval and
script tags (strict CSP).


======== docs/api.md ========

# API guide

LANventory has a JSON REST API under `/api/v1`. The OpenAPI 3.1 specification is the single source
of truth: it is served at `/api/openapi.json` (and `/api/openapi.yaml`), rendered at `/api/` and
kept in the repository at [`internal/api/openapi.yaml`](../internal/api/openapi.yaml). Tests check
that every route is documented and vice versa, and call every endpoint – including error cases –
validating status code, content type and body against the specification
([ADR 0007](adr/0007-openapi-single-source-of-truth.md)). The API uses the same store functions and
validation as the web UI, so both enforce the same rules.

## Authentication

Users create tokens in the web UI under **Account → API tokens**; the secret is shown exactly once.

```
Authorization: Bearer lvk_3Fq9…
```

- The prefix `lvk_` (followed by 40 random characters) makes tokens easy to spot in logs and secret
  scanners. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored; a lost token cannot be recovered, only replaced.
- Tokens can expire (optional, in days) and be revoked at any time by their owner or an admin.
  Creating a token requires a recent authentication in the web UI.
- A token acts as **its owner**, with at most the owner's *current* rights: the effective
  permission is the token's scope AND the owner's role and flags at request time. Demoting or
  disabling the owner takes effect immediately (a disabled owner makes the token invalid).
- A logged-in browser session may call the API as well (complete sessions only, not one that still
  waits for a second factor). Rights follow the role like in the UI; unsafe methods need the header
  `X-CSRF-Token` with the session's token and a same-origin request. If the MFA policy requires a
  second factor the user lacks, the API answers 403 `mfa_required`.
- Requests are rate limited per token (`api.rate_limit`, `api.rate_burst`); excess requests get
  HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`.

### Scopes

| Scope | Grants | Also needs the owner to be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read:assets` | read locations, categories and assets (including the DGUV state of an asset) | any role |
| `write:assets` | create, update and delete assets and locations | editor; deleting an asset: admin |
| `read:inspections` | read inspections and the due overview | any role |
| `write:inspections` | record inspections, delete an inspection | `can_inspect` flag; deleting: admin |

Categories are read-only in API v1; admins manage categories and fields in the web UI.
`GET /api/v1/me` needs no scope and shows who you are and which scopes are effective right now.

## Conventions

- JSON, snake_case. Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC, dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, numbers are JSON numbers.
- Custom field values are an object `fields` keyed by the field key: `number` fields as numbers (the
  unit is in the category's field definition), `bool` as booleans, `text`, `date` and `select` as
  strings. Unset fields are absent.
- Lists return `{"items": [...], "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total": 123}`. Parameters: `page`
  (from 1) and `per_page` (default 50, maximum 200). A page past the end is empty.
- `PATCH` is a partial update: only the sent properties change, `null` clears optional values. The
  inventory number of an asset cannot change (422 `immutable`). Another `category_id` moves the
  asset: custom values carry over to fields with the same key (when valid for the new type), others
  are dropped; `fields` then refer to the new category, whose required fields must be filled. The
  number and the inspections stay; the move is in the asset history.
- Without `inventory_no`, a new asset gets the next number (of its category prefix, if the format
  uses one; the prefix may be empty), generated from
  `inventory.number_format`; a manual number must be unique.
- Every change is written to the audit log with the token's owner as actor and `"via": "api"` plus
  the token ID (never the token).

## Errors

Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`:

```json
{"type": "urn:lanventory:problem:validation_failed", "title": "Unprocessable Entity", "status": 422,
 "code": "validation_failed", "detail": "the request is well-formed but its values are invalid",
 "errors": {"name": "required", "fields.length": "invalid_number"}}
```

| Status | `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_parameter`, `invalid_json` | bad query parameter; body is not one JSON object |
| 401 | `invalid_token`, `unauthorized` | token unknown, revoked, expired or owner disabled; no (complete) session |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | the token lacks the scope |
| 403 | `forbidden` | the owner's current role or flags do not allow it |
| 403 | `csrf_failed`, `mfa_required` | session without CSRF header or same origin; second factor missing |
| 404 | `not_found` | no such resource or endpoint |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | for example writing categories |
| 409 | `conflict` | deleting a location that assets use |
| 413, 415 | `payload_too_large`, `unsupported_media_type` | body over 1 MiB; not `application/json` |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | invalid values; `errors` maps field names (custom fields as `fields.<key>`) to codes such as `required`, `too_long`, `taken`, `invalid_date`, `invalid_number`, `invalid_option`, `invalid_location`, `invalid_status`, `immutable`, `unknown_field`, `invalid_type` |
| 422 | `not_inspectable`, `asset_inactive` | inspection of an asset whose category needs no DGUV V3, or that is retired or lost |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | per-token rate limit |

## Endpoints

| Method & path | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/me` | – | Acting user, authentication kind, token, effective scopes |
| `GET /api/v1/locations`, `GET /locations/{id}` | read:assets | Locations (flat list, with asset counts) |
| `POST /api/v1/locations`, `PATCH /locations/{id}`, `DELETE /locations/{id}` | write:assets | Create, change, delete (409 while assets use it) |
| `GET /api/v1/categories`, `GET /categories/{id}` | read:assets | Categories with field definitions, `dguv_required`, `dguv_interval_months` |
| `GET /api/v1/assets` | read:assets | List and search: `q`, `category`, `location`, `status`, `f_<key>` (with `category`), `sort`, `dir` |
| `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}`, `GET /assets/by-number/{inventory_no}` | read:assets | One asset with `fields` and `dguv` (`state`, `last_inspected_on`, `next_due`) |
| `POST /api/v1/assets`, `PATCH /assets/{id}` | write:assets | Create (`category_id`, `name` required), partial update |
| `PATCH /api/v1/assets` | write:assets | Bulk update: `ids` (at most 1000), `changes`, `dry_run`; all or nothing (see below) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/assets/{id}` | write:assets, admin | Delete an asset (retiring it with `status: retired` keeps the history) |
| `GET /api/v1/inspections` | read:inspections | List: `from`, `to`, `result`, `category`, `location`, `asset`, `inspector` |
| `GET /api/v1/inspections/{id}`, `GET /assets/{id}/inspections` | read:inspections | One inspection; the inspections of an asset |
| `GET /api/v1/inspections/due` | read:inspections | Overdue, due within 30 days, never inspected: `state`, `category`, `location` |
| `POST /api/v1/assets/{id}/inspections` | write:inspections, `can_inspect` | Record an inspection |
| `DELETE /api/v1/inspections/{id}` | write:inspections, admin | Delete an inspection (audited) |

Inspections are records and cannot be edited. They follow the rules of the web form: only assets of
categories that require DGUV V3 and that are not retired or lost; the date may not be more than one day
in the future; measurements (`pe_resistance_ohm`, `insulation_mohm`, `leakage_ma` for the protective
conductor / leakage current, `touch_ma` for the touch current) are optional non-negative numbers.
A reading beyond the instrument's range is a number plus a qualifier property `pe_resistance_cmp`,
`insulation_cmp`, `leakage_cmp` or `touch_cmp` (`""`, `"<"`, `">"`); for convenience the measurement
may also be a string such as `">299"` or `"< 0,01"`, which sets the qualifier (a contradicting
explicit one is a 422 `invalid_cmp`). Further optional properties: `reason` (`initial`, `repeat`,
`repair`), `leakage_method` (`direct`, `differential`, `alternative`), `test_device`,
`test_device_id` and `test_device_calibrated_until` (date). Responses always contain all of them
(empty string, or null for numbers and the date, when not recorded). Guidance compares the numbers as they are. `inspected_on` defaults to today (UTC) and `inspector_name` to the token owner.
LANventory never derives pass or fail from measurements; `guidance` lists non-binding hints. A failed
result sets an active asset to defective when `set_defective` is `true`; a passed result sets a
defective asset back to active when `set_active` is `true`. The response contains `asset_status`
(`previous`, `current`). LANventory documents inspections; it does not replace a qualified electrician.

## Examples

```bash
export TOKEN=lvk_...
BASE=https://inventory.example

# who am I, and what may I do?
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/api/v1/me

# search assets
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/api/v1/assets?q=drum&status=active&per_page=20"

# look up a label scan
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/api/v1/assets/by-number/KT-00012

# create an asset (inventory number generated)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"category_id": 2, "name": "Drum 25 m", "location_id": 1, "fields": {"length": 25}}' \
  $BASE/api/v1/assets

# mark it defective
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "defective"}' $BASE/api/v1/assets/12

# move three assets to location 3 and retire them in one call (add "dry_run": true to only check)
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ids": [12, 13, 14], "changes": {"location_id": 3, "status": "retired"}}' $BASE/api/v1/assets

# record a DGUV V3 inspection
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"result": "pass", "protection_class": "I", "visual_ok": true, "function_ok": true, "pe_resistance_ohm": 0.12, "insulation_mohm": ">299", "touch_ma": 0.2, "reason": "repeat"}' \
  $BASE/api/v1/assets/12/inspections

# what is overdue?
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/api/v1/inspections/due?state=overdue"
```


======== docs/configuration.md ========

# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by go run ./tools/gendocs from internal/config/config.go. Do not edit by hand. -->

`config.yaml` holds process-level settings only. Users, categories and assets live in the
database. `lanventory config init` writes an example and creates `secret.key`; the same file is
[config.example.yaml](config.example.yaml). The file is found with `-c/--config`, else
`LANVENTORY_CONFIG`, else `/etc/lanventory/config.yaml`.

- Relative paths are relative to the directory of the configuration file.
- Unknown keys are ignored. For editor validation, point your YAML language server at
  [config.schema.json](config.schema.json).
- Changes take effect after a restart.
- Environment variables override: `LANVENTORY_LISTEN` (`listen`), `LANVENTORY_PUBLIC_URL`
  (`public_url`) and `LANVENTORY_LOG_LEVEL` (`log.level`).

Command line: `lanventory server`, `config init [--force]`, `migrate`, `backup [file]`, `user create|passwd|list|delete`, `version`.
Passwords are read from the terminal, or from stdin when piped (one line), and need at least 10
characters. `backup` writes a consistent copy with `VACUUM INTO` while the server runs.

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string | `127.0.0.1:9060` | The HTTP listen address, e.g. "127.0.0.1:9060". |
| `public_url` | string | `http://127.0.0.1:9060` | The externally visible base URL (scheme, host and port, no path). If it starts with https://, session cookies are marked Secure. Requests whose Origin header differs from it are rejected. |
| `trusted_proxies` | []string | `[127.0.0.1, ::1]` | The proxy IPs or networks whose X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers are trusted for client IPs (lockout, audit log). |
| `secret_key_file` | string | `secret.key` | The file with the AES-256 key that encrypts secrets in the database (64 hex characters). It is created if missing. |

## `storage` – Configures the SQLite database

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storage.path` | string | `data/lanventory.db` | The SQLite database file. Its directory is created if missing. |

## `log` – Configures logging

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `log.level` | string | `info` | The minimum log level: debug, info, warn or error. Allowed: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. |
| `log.format` | string | `text` | The log output format: text or json. Allowed: `text`, `json`. |

## `tls` – Enables the built-in TLS listener; usually a reverse proxy does this

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tls.cert_file` | string | `–` | The PEM certificate (chain). Set together with tls.key_file. |
| `tls.key_file` | string | `–` | The PEM private key. |

## `inventory` – Configures inventory behavior (number format of generated inventory numbers)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory.number_format` | string | `{prefix}-{seq:05}` | The template of automatically assigned inventory numbers: {prefix} is the category prefix, {seq:05} the running number with the given minimum width. Without {prefix} (for example "{seq:04}" for 0001, 0002, …) all categories share one running number; a category without prefix drops {prefix} and the separator after it. |

## `organization` – Describes who runs this instance; it appears on printed inspection protocols

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `organization.name` | string | `–` | Printed in the header of inspection protocols, for example the name of your association or company. Optional; empty prints no name. |

## `api` – Configures the REST API under /api/v1

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.rate_limit` | float | `10` | The sustained number of API requests per second for each API token (browser sessions are limited per user). Excess requests get HTTP 429. |
| `api.rate_burst` | int | `30` | The number of API requests a token may send at once before RateLimit applies. |


======== docs/security.md ========

# Security

## Assets

- User accounts and their roles.
- The inventory, including DGUV V3 inspection records.
- `secret.key`, which protects secrets stored in the database (TOTP secrets) and keys the MACs of
  recovery codes.

## Threats

| ID | Threat |
|---|---|
| T1 | Guessing or stealing passwords (brute force, user enumeration) |
| T2 | Session theft or fixation |
| T3 | Cross-site request forgery and clickjacking |
| T4 | Script injection through stored data (XSS) |
| T5 | Theft of the database file |
| T6 | Privilege escalation between roles |
| T7 | Misuse or leakage of API tokens |

## Mitigations

### Passwords and login (T1)

- Argon2id (m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1), minimum length 10.
- Five failed logins within 10 minutes lock the client IP and the user name for 5 minutes.
  Failures for unknown users take the same time as for known ones (dummy hash).
- Re-entering the own password is required to create users or reset passwords (also rate
  limited).

### Second factors (T1, T2)

- TOTP (RFC 6238, ±30 s): the secret is AES-GCM encrypted (associated data binds it to the
  user), shown only during enrollment, and every time step is accepted only once (conditional
  update, safe against parallel requests).
- Recovery codes: 10 × ~49 bits, shown once, stored as HMAC-SHA256 under a subkey of
  `secret.key`, single use.
- Passkeys (WebAuthn, `go-webauthn`): relying-party ID and the single accepted origin come from
  `public_url`; only public keys are stored; sign-count anomalies are flagged on the security
  page. Ceremonies are single use, bound to purpose and user and expire after 5 minutes.
  Passwordless login and passkey re-authentication require user verification (PIN/biometrics),
  so a passkey alone is two factors.
- After a correct password a user with a second factor only gets a *pending* session (5
  minutes, new session ID on completion) that reaches nothing but the second-factor page.
  Wrong codes count toward the same lockout as wrong passwords.
- Policy: admins can require a second factor for admins or everyone; affected users without
  one can only reach the enrollment pages, and cannot remove their last factor.
- Changing second factors, the policy, or another user's MFA requires an authentication younger
  than 10 minutes (passkey, or password plus code). Admins can reset a user's MFA (web or
  `lanventory user reset-mfa`), which also ends that user's sessions.
- All MFA events go to the audit log, never with secrets or codes.

### Sessions (T2, T3)

- The cookie holds a random token; only its SHA-256 is stored. A new session is created on
  every login. Sessions end on password change, disabling and deletion of the user.
- Cookie flags: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` with an `https://` `public_url`.
- Every state-changing request needs the session's CSRF token and a same-origin `Origin`
  (`null` and foreign origins are rejected, `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` too).
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`.

### Content (T4)

- Strict CSP: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; …; object-src 'none'`.
  Templates contain no inline scripts, styles or event handlers (a test checks this).
- All output goes through `html/template`.

### Stored secrets (T5)

- Secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, bound to associated data. The key is in a separate
  file (`secret.key`, mode 0600/0640), so a copy of the database alone does not reveal them.
  Password hashes are Argon2id.
- The audit log never contains secrets.

### Roles (T6)

- Roles are checked in the router, not only in the UI. The last enabled admin cannot be
  demoted, disabled or deleted.

### API tokens (T3, T6, T7)

- A token is `lvk_` plus 40 random base62 characters (~238 bits), shown once; only its SHA-256
  hash is stored (a database copy does not reveal usable tokens). Tokens never appear in logs,
  the audit log (only name, prefix and token ID) or later responses.
- A token acts as its owner and is limited by scopes; the effective permission is scope AND the
  owner's current role and flags, so demoting or disabling the owner takes effect at once.
  Revoked, expired and disabled-owner tokens are rejected with 401. Category writes are not
  exposed. Creating a token requires a recent authentication; users revoke their own tokens,
  admins any.
- Bearer requests carry no ambient credentials, so they need no CSRF token. Browser sessions
  calling the API need `X-CSRF-Token` and a same-origin request, are refused while a second
  factor is pending and follow the MFA policy.
- Per-token rate limit (`api.rate_limit`, `api.rate_burst`). Use HTTPS: a bearer token is a
  password in transit.

### CSV import and export

- Exports guard every cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR with a leading
  apostrophe (formula injection in spreadsheets); the import removes it again.
- The import is limited to editors; the upload (5 MB, 20 000 rows, 100 columns) is parsed in
  memory and kept there only between the wizard steps: random token bound to user and session,
  one upload per user, 30 minutes, never written to disk. Cells are untrusted text: they are
  validated like form input and escaped when shown. Imports are audited (`asset.import`,
  `asset.create`/`asset.update` with `via: import`).

## Residual risks

- A leaked token works until it expires or is revoked; give tokens the fewest scopes and an expiry.
- Without HTTPS passwords are visible on the network (the UI warns).
- Second factors are optional unless an admin sets the policy.
- WebAuthn ceremonies live in memory: a restart cancels running ones (users simply retry).
- Anyone with root on the host can read `secret.key` and the database.
- Losing `secret.key` makes TOTP secrets unreadable and recovery codes unusable; back it up
  together with the database.


======== internal/api/openapi.yaml ========

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: LANventory API
  version: "1.0"
  summary: Inventory of LAN party equipment with DGUV V3 inspections.
  description: |
    LANventory manages assets (single physical items) with an inventory number, a category with
    configurable fields, a location and a status, and records DGUV V3 electrical inspections.
    This API is the JSON interface to the same data and rules as the web UI.

    Authentication: send `Authorization: Bearer lvk_...`. Tokens are created in the web UI under
    Account > API tokens; the secret is shown once. A token acts as its owner with at most the
    owner's current role, limited by its scopes: `read:assets` (locations, categories, assets),
    `write:assets` (create, update and delete assets and locations; deleting an asset needs an
    admin owner; categories are read-only in v1), `read:inspections`, `write:inspections` (record
    inspections; needs an owner with the can_inspect flag; deleting one needs an admin owner).
    A logged-in browser session also works (role based like the UI); unsafe methods then need the
    header `X-CSRF-Token` and a same-origin request.

    Conventions:
    - JSON with snake_case names. Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC, dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`,
      numbers are JSON numbers. Custom field values are in the object `fields` keyed by the field
      key: number fields as numbers, bool fields as booleans, text, date and select as strings.
    - Lists return `{items, page, per_page, total}` and take `page` (from 1) and `per_page`
      (default 50, maximum 200). A page past the end is empty.
    - Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Invalid values yield
      HTTP 422 `validation_failed` with `errors`, a map from field name to a short code
      (`required`, `too_long`, `taken`, `invalid_date`, `invalid_option`, `immutable`, ...);
      custom fields are named `fields.<key>`.
    - Updates are partial (PATCH): only the sent properties change. `null` clears optional values.
    - Every change is written to the audit log with the token's owner as actor and `via: api`.
    - The rate limit applies per token (HTTP 429, `Retry-After`).
  license:
    name: MIT
    identifier: MIT
servers:
  - url: /
security:
  - bearer: []
tags:
  - name: locations
  - name: categories
  - name: assets
  - name: inspections
  - name: account

paths:
  /api/v1/me:
    get:
      tags: [account]
      operationId: getMe
      summary: Who am I
      x-required: "any valid token or session"
      description: |
        Returns the acting user, how the request was authenticated and the scopes that are effective right now.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Me"}
              example: {user: {id: 3, username: alice, role: editor, can_inspect: true}, auth: token, token: {id: 7, name: label-printer, prefix: lvk_ab12, scopes: [read:assets, write:assets], expires_at: null}, effective_scopes: [read:assets, write:assets]}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://inventory.example/api/v1/me\""
  /api/v1/locations:
    get:
      tags: [locations]
      operationId: listLocations
      summary: List locations
      x-required: "scope read:assets"
      description: |
        Locations are a flat list, ordered by name.
      parameters:
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/page"}
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/per_page"}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/LocationList"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://inventory.example/api/v1/locations\""
    post:
      tags: [locations]
      operationId: createLocation
      summary: Create a location
      x-required: "scope write:assets, role editor"
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/LocationInput"}
            example: {name: "Storage 3", description: ""}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created; the Location header has the URL
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Location"}
              example: {id: 1, name: "Storage 1", description: "Basement", asset_count: 42, created_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z", updated_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "415": {$ref: "#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType"}
        "422": {$ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationFailed"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"name\":\"Storage 3\"}' https://inventory.example/api/v1/locations"
  /api/v1/locations/{id}:
    get:
      tags: [locations]
      operationId: getLocation
      summary: Get a location
      x-required: "scope read:assets"
      parameters:
        - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Location"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
    patch:
      tags: [locations]
      operationId: updateLocation
      summary: Change a location
      x-required: "scope write:assets, role editor"
      parameters:
        - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/LocationInput"}
            example: {description: "Basement, left"}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Location"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}
        "415": {$ref: "#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType"}
        "422": {$ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationFailed"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
    delete:
      tags: [locations]
      operationId: deleteLocation
      summary: Delete a location
      x-required: "scope write:assets, role editor"
      description: |
        Refused with 409 while assets use the location.
      parameters:
        - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
      responses:
        "204": {description: Deleted}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}
        "409": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
  /api/v1/categories:
    get:
      tags: [categories]
      operationId: listCategories
      summary: List categories
      x-required: "scope read:assets"
      description: |
        Categories with their field definitions. Categories are read-only in API v1; admins manage them in the web UI.
      parameters:
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/page"}
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/per_page"}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/CategoryList"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://inventory.example/api/v1/categories\""

        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}

  /api/v1/assets:
    get:
      tags: [assets]
      operationId: listAssets
      summary: List and search assets
      x-required: "scope read:assets"
      description: |
        The list items carry no `dguv` object; fetch one asset for its inspection state.
      parameters:
        - {name: q, in: query, description: "Search words; each must match number, name, serial number, manufacturer, model or a field value.", schema: {type: string}}
        - {name: category, in: query, description: Category ID., schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
        - {name: location, in: query, description: Location ID., schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
        - {name: status, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [active, defective, retired, lost]}}
        - {name: "f_<key>", in: query, description: "Filter by a custom field of the chosen category, for example f_color=red. Needs category. Booleans as true or false.", schema: {type: string}}
        - {name: sort, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [inventory_no, name, category, location, status, updated], default: inventory_no}}
        - {name: dir, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [asc, desc], default: asc}}
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/page"}
        - {$ref: "#/components/parameters/per_page"}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/AssetList"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets?q=drum&status=active&per_page=20\""
    post:
      tags: [assets]
      operationId: createAsset
      summary: Create an asset
      x-required: "scope write:assets, role editor"
      description: |
        `category_id` and `name` are required. Without `inventory_no` the number is generated from the configured format.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/AssetCreate"}
            example: {category_id: 2, name: "Drum 25 m", location_id: 1, fields: {length: 25}}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created; the Location header has the URL
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Asset"}
              example: {id: 12, inventory_no: KT-00012, category_id: 2, category_name: "Cable drum", name: "Drum 25 m", serial_no: "", manufacturer: "", model: "", location_id: 1, location_name: "Storage 1", status: active, note: "", purchase_date: "2025-03-01", dguv_interval_months: null, fields: {length: 25}, dguv: {required: true, state: soon, last_inspected_on: "2025-12-01", next_due: "2026-12-01"}, created_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z", updated_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "415": {$ref: "#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType"}
        "422": {$ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationFailed"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"category_id\":2,\"name\":\"Drum 25 m\",\"fields\":{\"length\":25}}' https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets"
    patch:
      tags: [assets]
      operationId: bulkUpdateAssets
      summary: Change several assets at once
      x-required: "scope write:assets, role editor"
      description: |
        Applies the same `changes` to the assets in `ids` (at most 1000, duplicates are ignored) in one transaction: all or nothing. With `dry_run: true` everything is checked and computed, nothing is written and no audit entries are made. `name`, `serial_no` and `inventory_no` cannot be changed in bulk (422 `not_allowed`), unknown keys give 422 `unknown_field`. Another `category_id` moves every asset (values carry over by field key; the response shows the result). `fields` are keyed by field key and must exist in the target category (the new one, else the assets' own); `null` clears a value. With `note_append` the `note` is added as a new line instead of replacing the note. Validation problems are reported per asset as `"<asset id>.<property>"` (for example `"12.fields.length_m": required`); request-level problems as `ids` or `changes.<property>`.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/BulkAssetUpdate"}
            example: {ids: [12, 13, 14], changes: {location_id: 3, status: active}, dry_run: false}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Applied (or, with `dry_run`, what would happen). `updated` counts the assets that actually change; `items` has every selected asset in the state after the change.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/BulkAssetResult"}
              example: {updated: 1, dry_run: false, items: [{id: 12, inventory_no: KT-00012, category_id: 2, category_name: "Cable drum", name: "Drum 25 m", serial_no: "", manufacturer: "", model: "", location_id: 3, location_name: "Storage 2", status: active, note: "", purchase_date: null, dguv_interval_months: null, fields: {length: 25}, dguv: {required: true, state: soon, last_inspected_on: "2025-12-01", next_due: "2026-12-01"}, created_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z", updated_at: "2026-11-02T08:30:00Z"}]}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "415": {$ref: "#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType"}
        "422":
          description: Invalid request or values; nothing was changed
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
              example: {type: "urn:lanventory:problem:validation_failed", title: Unprocessable Entity, status: 422, code: validation_failed, detail: "the request is well-formed but its values are invalid", errors: {"12.fields.length_m": required, "13.fields.length_m": required}}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
        "500": {$ref: "#/components/responses/InternalError"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: "curl -X PATCH -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"ids\":[12,13],\"changes\":{\"status\":\"retired\"}}' https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets"
